course_summary:
ISEN 631 | Cognitive Systems Engineering | Spring 2026
Instructor: Thomas Ferris | tferris@tamu.edu
Grading: Reading responses and Discussion board [20%], Midterm Exam [25%], Final Exam [25%], Project proposal [1.5%], Front end analysis report [7.5%], Task analysis description and report [9%], Solution and evaluation report [9%], In-class presentation [3%] — A: 90-100%, B: 80-89%, C: 70-79%, D: 60-69%, F: 59% and lower
Topics: Woods & Roth, Wilson, Wickens et al., Bisantz & Roth, Ferris & Shepley, Rasmussen, Reason, Lee & See, Ferris et al., Norman, Smith et al., Vicente, Woods, Ferris & Sarter, Kahneman & Klein, Gigerenzer & Goldstein, Lottridge et al., NICU incubator design, Skill-Rule-Knowledge Framework, Gulfs of Execution, Gulfs of Evaluation, Ecological Interface Design, Dynamic fault management, Ironies of automation, Cognitive Systems Engineering (CSE), sociotechnical systems engineering, human-automation interaction models, Trust in human-automation systems, system design strategies, resilience engineering principles, error management techniques, Cognitive Task Analysis, Task analysis techniques, human error models, human error classification, design-induced error, Decision Making models, Decision Support Systems, qualitative data collection, formal task analytical methodologies, in situ data collection, observational techniques, front end analysis, human-centered design methods, user-centered design techniques, research methods, evaluation methods, concept mapping, display/interface design to support attention, task management, technology development, software tool, external memory aid, information visualization, procedural change, training method, usability study, focus groups, interviews, surveys, mini-experiments, human cognitive functions, perception, attention, memory, decision-making, problem-solving, communication, planning, human behavioral modes, human performance, directed attention, emotion factors, stress factors, artifacts, displays, social interaction, joint human-machine systems, humans and technologies interact, cognitive work, sociotechnical systems, system elements, system interactions, system breakdowns, system tasks, system functions, subtasks, existing technology, humansystems interaction problems, human-centered redesign solutions, underlying theory, current hot topics, trends in cognitive systems engineering research, creativity, communication skills, analysis and design methods, potential system improvements
Tools: Canvas, Slack
Prerequisites: ISEN 635, ISEN 430/ISEN 630, or approval of instructor

headers.text: A. An insightful question about the reading. Time permitting, I will address as many of these questions as I can in lecture, and classmates will have a chance to respond as well.
B. A comment about how the reading relates to other course concepts or to an example/anecdote from your own life experience.
